answer: Stop sybils with a falcon, a fable, and a vine. Each identity flies one falcon: a memory-hard sequential proof chained to its own past receipts, so one machine cannot fly two falcon flights at once. Each identity publishes a fable, a chained history of past epochs; verifiers spot-check random links, so a farm faking many fable histories must keep them pairwise consistent, and exposure grows like N squared. A new identity grafts onto a vine rooted in a staked sponsor; the vine weight is capped by its root, and if any leaf proves fake the root stake burns.
